_about: PARKED (Combat, 2026-10-23; docs/combat/biomes.md section 2). The signature's variant by the biome under the defender, one row a biome: its name, how its beam bites the terrain and structures, what it leaves behind, and its outcome flavour. It replaces the tables that hold this today: data/combat/templates.json beam.variants (the names), sim/world/crater.gd SCORCH_VARIANT (depth and width factors), the variant branches in sim/director/beam.gd sampleBeam (dust, sparks, fire), and beam.gd's unused copy const VARIANT (to delete on the switch). render/vfx/debris.gd also branches by the variant's name (glass flecks, spray puffs, larger embers); it keeps reading the name, which does not change. The seven rows marked asBuilt carry today's numbers exactly, so reading this file instead of the three is bit-identical; only the new rows add behaviour. Biome keys are the names WorldBiomes.biomeAt returns; the eight new keys are provisional until World names its ids. Names are working labels until Legal screens them and Orb picks. The file picks what the beam carves, so it goes into DirData.dataHash as enders.json does.

fields.name: the label in the director's feed and the banner: upper case, place or material plus effect (Legal RL-008's pattern)
fields.scorch: [depth factor, width factor] on the groove (crater.gd: depth (D0 + D_P x P) x depth factor, half width (HW0 + HW_P x P) x width factor)
fields.structMul: times the beam's structure bite (b.sf) for the whole beam. The variant is picked once, when the signature is planned, from the biome under the defender (as planBeam does today), and holds for the whole path
fields.trees: what the beam does to trees on its path: area (today's area damage), burn, fell (fall inward across the groove), snap (crowns drop), none
fields.fx: VFX's keys: dust colour, sparks, fire (sampleBeam's branches today; fire.withinAbove is in the prototype's units, times SimConst.WS as sampleBeam reads it); the other flags are new looks for VFX. Positions and counts stay in the code as today (one dust puff at g + 8 and the sparks at g + 6, inside the beam's reach test; one fire at g, under its own height test): the table carries only what varies
fields.aftermath: what the scar leaves for the rest of the fight (World's to build): null, or a kind from the aftermath table with its numbers. It is laid only on the groove's columns whose biome is the variant's own; where the beam carves on into another biome the groove there is plain
fields.outcomes: the flavour of each outcome here. Presentation unless the line starts with 'rule:', which marks a mechanical twist for Encounter and World

aftermath.clearing: the canopy over the groove is gone for the match: the strip no longer counts as forest cover, and the trees lie across it as fallen trunks (props a ricochet can plant on)
aftermath.fireLine: dry grass burns outward from the groove: spreads 1 column each spreadTicks for durTicks, up to reachCols each side; burns props and grass; no damage to fighters unless Game Design rules it
aftermath.heave: the groove's rim is thrown up as frozen plates rimMul x the berm: ground a slide stops against (World's WALL rule) and a slope a ricochet plants on
aftermath.snowDump: snow off the trees refills refill of the groove's depth over durTicks: a shallower scar under a powder curtain
aftermath.flood: the groove fills with water to the water table (wetland) or the sea (coast, where its floor is below sea level within seaCols of open water): a water trench under the ocean rules (sink, skim, submerge)
aftermath.scree: on a slope steeper than minSlope, rubble runs downhill from the groove up to reachCols over durTicks: a rubble strip (surface rubble: a slide over it tumbles)
aftermath.ember: the groove glows: its surface reads ember for durTicks, then crust; it lights props and grass; no damage to fighters unless Game Design rules it
aftermath.glaze: meltwater refreezes in the groove: its surface reads ice for the rest of the match (a slick strip)
aftermath.split: every floe the path crosses breaks at the path into two plates that drift gapBh apart: a lead of open water (a real gap in the ground)

ocean.name: HORIZON CLEAVE
ocean._rename: TIDE CLEAVE proposed (RL-006: 'Horizon' is a brand)

outcomes.CLASH: the beams meet over a standing column of spray
outcomes.GUARD: the guard is driven back across the surface, a wake behind
outcomes.DODGE: the dodge throws up a sheet of spray
outcomes.HIT: he is driven under and surfaces in a boil of foam
outcomes.ESCAPE: he breaks away low along the water, skimming

outcomes.CLASH: the meeting point blows out the windows of the street below
outcomes.GUARD: the guard skids back down the street on paving, sparks under the heels
outcomes.DODGE: the dodge goes up a facade and off it
outcomes.HIT: he is carried into the tower behind the scar
outcomes.ESCAPE: he breaks away between the towers, low along the street
